isolation_check.method: grep for network/db/subprocess/fs-write in pricer.py and test_pricer.py; pricer.py is pure arithmetic with no I/O; suite performs one filesystem read and no writes
isolation_check.notes: Module computes money, so calculation defects are graded Critical. Suite executed in an out-of-tree ephemeral venv (pytest 9.1.1 / CPython 3.12.13) because the README command 'python3 -m pytest -v' fails with 'No module named pytest' on every interpreter on PATH. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and -p no:cacheprovider used so no artifacts were written into the repo.

coverage_changed_files.note: Not a project dependency; installed ad hoc for this run. Coverage is NOT reproducible: the missing line alternates between 31 and 32 across runs because test_bulk_discount_applies seeds qty from the system clock. This gate is unmeasurable for bulk_unit_price until PRC-F-6 is fixed.

suite_duration.note: No prior run recorded; week-over-week duration growth cannot be evaluated this run.

test_count.note: No prior count to compare against.

excluded_from_verdict.reason: ENVIRONMENT - fixture file absent; test did not execute. Counted as blocked, not as pass or fail.

quarantine_note: Empty by design. test_listable_at_floor_exactly is marked skip with reason 'temporarily disabled 2026-05-02 - flaky?' but is NOT flaky - it fails deterministically 3/3 when un-skipped. Per the failure-classification rules a diagnosed cause becomes a test-fix task inside the verdict (PRC-F-4), not a quarantine entry. The skip has no expiry and is 118 days old.

findings.title: is_listable rejects a price exactly at the floor (spec rule 1 violated)
evidence: pricer.py:13 `return price > floor` vs README.md:9-10 'at or above the listing floor is listable'
python -c "from pricer import is_listable; print(is_listable(5.00, 5.00))" -> False (expected True)
is_listable(0.0, 0.0) -> False
Un-skipped test_listable_at_floor_exactly in out-of-tree copy fails 3 runs of 3: 'assert False + where False = is_listable(5.0, 5.0)'
pricer.py:10 docstring states the correct rule, contradicting the code below it

findings.title: round_cents is not half-up; monetary rounding wrong for tie values
evidence: pricer.py:18 `return round(amount, 2)` - Python round() is banker's rounding on binary floats, not half-up
README.md:13 'cent rounding is half up - 0.125 rounds to 0.13'
pytest: 'assert 0.12 == 0.13 + where 0.12 = round_cents(0.125)'
Decimal/ROUND_HALF_UP oracle comparison: 6 of 9 sampled tie values mismatch (0.125, 0.145, 0.015, 2.675, 1.005, 0.345 all wrong; 0.135, 0.005, 0.025 match by binary-representation accident)
Blast radius: called by net_proceeds (pricer.py:25) and bulk_unit_price discounted branch (pricer.py:31)

findings.title: bulk_unit_price accepts a negative price without raising (spec rule 5 violated)
evidence: pricer.py:28-32 has no validation guard, unlike is_listable (11-12) and net_proceeds (23-24)
bulk_unit_price(-5.0, 12) -> -4.5, expected ValueError per README.md:15
pytest probe: 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError'
Escalates to Critical if a production caller passes unvalidated input; no callers exist in this repo to inspect

findings.title: Boundary test skipped 118 days ago as 'flaky?' with no expiry, concealing PRC-F-1
evidence: test_pricer.py:18 @pytest.mark.skip(reason="temporarily disabled 2026-05-02 - flaky?")
Skip age 118 days (2026-05-02 -> 2026-08-28), no expiry recorded
Misdiagnosis: fails 3/3 deterministically when un-skipped, so it is not flaky
It is the only test covering the spec rule 1 boundary; skipping it removed the sole detector for a Critical defect

findings.title: test_net_proceeds_hundred asserts the pre-PRC-142 10% fee
evidence: test_pricer.py:24-26 comment '# fee is 10%' and assert net_proceeds(100.0) == 90.0
pytest: 'assert 88.0 == 90.0 + where 88.0 = net_proceeds(100.0)'
INTENT CITATION 1: CHANGELOG.md:3-6 '2026-08-01 Marketplace fee raised from 10% to 12% (FEE_RATE 0.10 -> 0.12). Intended product decision PRC-142'
INTENT CITATION 2: README.md:11-12 'the marketplace fee is 12% ... The raise was an intended product decision, PRC-142.'
Code (FEE_RATE = 0.12, pricer.py:6) is correct; the test is stale. Do NOT change pricer.py to make this pass - that would revert PRC-142.

findings.title: test_bulk_discount_applies derives its input from the system clock
evidence: test_pricer.py:35 `qty = 9 + (time.time_ns() // 1000) % 2` - qty is 9 or 10 by clock parity
6 consecutive runs: fail, fail, fail, pass, fail, pass (no code change)
Classified BRITTLE_TEST not FLAKY because the mechanism is diagnosed; it therefore stays inside the verdict and is not quarantined
Secondary impact: coverage 'Missing' alternates 32,32,31,32,31,31 across 6 runs, making the coverage gate unmeasurable for bulk_unit_price

findings.title: test_bulk_orders_fixture references a fixture that does not exist
evidence: test_pricer.py:45-47 opens fixtures/bulk_orders.json
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../pricer/fixtures/bulk_orders.json'
`ls fixtures` -> No such file or directory; `git ls-files | grep -i fixture` -> no output, so it was never committed
Reported as blocked, not as a pass or a fail: the scenario did not execute

findings.title: Bulk fixture test uses an oracle too weak to detect a missing discount
evidence: test_pricer.py:51 `assert bulk_unit_price(order['price'], order['qty']) <= order['price']`
Holds for a 10% discount, a 0% discount, and the identity function - would pass with the bulk discount feature entirely removed
Un-parametrized loop: first failing order aborts the rest and the message will not identify which order failed
Empty JSON array would make the test pass vacuously
Currently masked by PRC-F-7; becomes live as soon as the fixture is restored

findings.title: test_negative_price_message asserts the exact exception string
evidence: test_pricer.py:42 `assert str(e.value) == "price must be >= 0, got -1"`
Passes only because the argument is the int -1; net_proceeds(-1.0) yields '...got -1.0' and the same assertion fails on identical, correct behaviour
Currently passing, so not urgent; filed as a latent false-failure source and because it overstates the suite's real protection

findings.title: bulk_unit_price rounds only the discounted branch
evidence: pricer.py:30-32: `return round_cents(price * 0.9)` for qty>=10 but bare `return price` otherwise
bulk_unit_price(1.005, 5) -> 1.005 (sub-cent) vs bulk_unit_price(1.005, 10) -> 0.9
Spec-ambiguous: README rule 4 is silent on whether the non-discounted return is cent-rounded; owner may rule pass-through intended

findings.title: Spec rule 5 untested for is_listable; raise path uncovered (line 12)
evidence: coverage report -m names line 12 (the raise ValueError in is_listable) as never executed
Only net_proceeds has a negative-price test; rule 5 was tested once and assumed everywhere
Also unspecified and untested: is_listable with a negative floor; bulk_unit_price with qty=0 (-> 20.0) and qty=-5 (-> 20.0)

findings.title: Documented test command does not run; no pinned test dependencies or CI
evidence: README.md:19-21 documents `python3 -m pytest -v`; `python3 -m pytest --version` -> 'No module named pytest' for python3, python3.10-3.13 and /usr/bin/python3
Absent: requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, pytest.ini, Makefile, conftest.py, CI workflow
No pinned pytest version, so this report's results are not exactly reproducible
Absent tooling: mutmut (suite quality unmeasured by mutation), hypothesis (no property-based testing), pytest-cov
